legal.disclaimerText: Overberg Skills Connect is a digital community noticeboard. Khulisa does not employ, recruit, recommend, vet, supervise or guarantee any person using this platform. Users are solely responsible for carrying out their own enquiries, obtaining references, requesting police clearance where appropriate, verifying qualifications and entering into any agreements. Khulisa accepts no responsibility for any loss, injury, damage, dispute or claim arising from introductions made through this platform.
legal.legalDisclaimerText: Hineni undertakes reasonable verification, vetting and safeguarding measures. However, Hineni cannot guarantee the conduct of third parties and accepts no liability for injury, loss, damage, misconduct, criminal activity or disputes arising from interactions between participants, mentors, employers, apprenticeship providers or other users of the platform. Participation is undertaken at the individual's own risk and subject to applicable South African law.

section1.title: 1. What this platform is
section1.p1: {{platform}} ("the platform") is a digital community noticeboard owned and operated by {{owner}}. It exists to allow people offering skills and people looking for help to find each other in their local community.

section2.title: 2. What Khulisa is not
section2.item3: Khulisa is not a labour broker.
section2.item4: Khulisa is not a recruitment agency.
section2.item9: Khulisa does not recommend any person.
section2.item10: Khulisa does not guarantee availability, suitability, safety, payment or work quality.

section3.title: 3. Your responsibilities
section3.p1: Users are solely responsible for conducting their own checks before entering into any agreement. This includes verifying identity, references, qualifications and work permits where applicable, and obtaining a police clearance certificate where appropriate.
section3.p2: Users are responsible for agreeing payment, work conditions and complying with all applicable legal obligations, including labour, tax and immigration law.
section3.p3: If you arrange contact or work through WhatsApp, telephone or any other channel, that arrangement is between the users involved. Keep your own records and do not share sensitive documents unless you are sure it is necessary and lawful.

section4.title: 4. Listings and conduct
section4.p1: You must only post information that is true and accurate, and you must be 18 or older to publish a listing. Khulisa may remove listings that breach these Terms, are misleading, fraudulent, offensive, illegal, or otherwise inappropriate.
section4.p2: You may not use the platform to harass, threaten, discriminate, scrape contact details, send spam, impersonate someone, collect information unlawfully, or attempt to bypass security controls.

section5.title: 5. Privacy and contact details
section5.p1: Telephone numbers are stored privately and are only shared with another user once you have explicitly approved their request. See our {{link}}.
section5.p2: The current WhatsApp integration is manual. The app may open WhatsApp with a prepared message, but the user must review and send that message themselves.

section6.title: 6. Reports and moderation
section6.p1: Users can report listings that appear unsafe, misleading or abusive. Reports are reviewed by admins. Khulisa may hide, edit, suspend or remove content or accounts where needed to protect users, comply with the law, or operate the platform responsibly.

section7.title: 7. Limitation of liability
section7.p1: To the maximum extent permitted by South African law, {{owner}} accepts no liability for any loss, injury, damage, dispute or claim arising from introductions made through this platform. See our {{link}}.

section9.title: 9. Governing law
section9.p1: These Terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of South Africa.

section1.title: 1. Who we are
section1.p1: {{platform}} ("we", "us") is operated by {{owner}}, the responsible party for the purposes of the Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013 (POPIA).

section2.title: 2. What information we collect
section2.item1: Account details such as your email address and sign-in information.
section2.item2: Listing details you provide, including name, town or area, skills, experience, availability, description and optional profile photograph.
section2.item3: Your telephone or WhatsApp number, stored privately unless you approve a contact request.
section2.item4: Contact request details, including requester name, contact number, message, status and decision date.
section2.item5: Reports submitted about listings, including reason, details, reporter account and optional contact details.
section2.item6: Technical records needed to run and secure the platform, such as timestamps, notifications and system logs.
section2.p1: Some future sections of the app refer to identity checks, parent consent, references, police clearance certificates, work permits, youth programmes or safeguarding records. Those sections are not live for this launch. If they are enabled later, this policy must be updated before that information is collected.

section3.title: 3. Why and how we use it
section3.p1: We use personal information to operate the skills noticeboard, publish listings, receive and manage contact requests, show in-app notifications, handle reports, prevent misuse, keep records of user choices, and respond to support, correction or deletion requests.
section3.p2: We process this information because it is needed to provide the platform, because users consent to specific sharing actions, because we have a legitimate interest in safety and abuse prevention, and because South African law may require us to keep or disclose certain records.

section4.title: 4. Contact details and WhatsApp
section4.p1Post: . It is only shared with another user when you explicitly approve their contact request. You can decline any request.
section4.p2: This launch uses manual WhatsApp links. When a contact request is approved or declined, the app may open WhatsApp with a prepared message for the user to review and send. WhatsApp messages are handled by WhatsApp/Meta under their own terms and privacy policies.

section5.title: 5. Sharing with service providers
section5.p1: We do not sell personal information. We may share limited information with service providers who help us operate the platform, such as hosting, authentication, database, email, analytics, security or communication services. We may also disclose information where required by law, court order, regulator request, or to protect users from harm, fraud or abuse.

section6.title: 6. Security and retention
section6.p1: We use access controls, private database rules, secure hosting and administrative restrictions to protect personal information. No online system is perfectly secure, so users should avoid posting sensitive details in public descriptions.
section6.p2: We keep active listing and account records while they are needed to provide the platform. Contact request records are reviewed and may be removed after they are no longer needed for the contact flow, dispute handling or legal record-keeping. Reviewed reports may be retained longer where needed for safety, abuse prevention or compliance.

section7.title: 7. Editing or removing your information
section7.p1Pre: You can hide or unhide your listing from your private management link or account. To permanently remove a listing, request deletion, request access to your information, or correct your information, contact us using the details on the

section8.title: 8. Your rights
section8.p1: Under POPIA you may request access to your personal information, ask us to correct or delete it, object to certain processing, withdraw consent where processing depends on consent, and complain to the Information Regulator. Contact us first so we can assist.

section9.title: 9. Children and special personal information
section9.p1: The public noticeboard is intended for adults. Users must not submit another person's identity documents, medical details, criminal history, child information, or other sensitive information unless a live feature specifically asks for it and the required consent and safeguards are in place.

section10.title: 10. Security incidents
section10.p1: If we reasonably believe that personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person, we will assess the incident and take the notification steps required by POPIA.

section11.title: 11. Contact
section11.p1Pre: For privacy questions, please use our
section11.p1Post: page. You may also contact the Information Regulator South Africa if you believe your POPIA rights have not been respected.

disclaimer.heading: Disclaimer
disclaimer.p1: Overberg Skills Connect is a digital community noticeboard. It exists only to help people offering skills and people looking for help to find each other. We are not a recruiter, employer, labour broker, agency or supervisor.
disclaimer.p2: We do not vet, verify, recommend or guarantee any person listed on this platform. We do not verify identities, qualifications, references, experience, work permits or police clearance. We do not confirm the accuracy of any information posted.
disclaimer.p3: You are responsible for carrying out your own enquiries before entering into any agreement. This includes — but is not limited to — verifying identity documents, requesting references, asking for a police clearance certificate where appropriate, agreeing payment and working conditions in writing, and complying with all applicable laws.
disclaimer.p4: Khulisa Group, Overberg Skills Connect and any related parties accept no responsibility for any loss, injury, damage, dispute or claim arising from introductions made through this platform.

meta.title: Safeguarding Policy — Hineni
meta.description: Hineni's Safeguarding Policy covering recruitment, mentoring, apprenticeships, conduct, reporting and digital safety for young people and vulnerable adults.

safeguarding.heading: Hineni Safeguarding Policy
safeguarding.intro: This policy sets out Hineni's commitment to the safety, dignity and wellbeing of every young person, vulnerable adult and participant who engages with our programmes, including apprenticeships, mentorships, work placements and community activities.
safeguarding.downloadTitle: Use your browser's 'Save as PDF' option

s1.title: Purpose
s1.p1: The purpose of this policy is to ensure that everyone who participates in Hineni's activities — including apprentices, mentees, mentors, volunteers, employers, apprenticeship providers, staff and community partners — is protected from harm, abuse, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.

s2.title: Scope
s2.item1: All Hineni staff, volunteers, mentors and board members.
s2.item2: All apprentices, mentees, young people and vulnerable adults engaging with Hineni.
s2.item3: All employers, farms, businesses, NPOs and households offering opportunities through Hineni.
s2.item4: All digital interactions on the Hineni platform.

s3.title: Commitment to safety
s3.p1: Hineni is committed to creating safe, respectful and inclusive environments. We recognise our duty of care toward children and vulnerable adults and we comply with applicable South African law, including:
s3.item2: The Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA), 4 of 2013;
s3.item3: The Criminal Law (Sexual Offences and Related Matters) Amendment Act, 32 of 2007;
s3.item4: The Basic Conditions of Employment Act and related labour legislation governing young workers;
s3.item5: The Sector Code on the prevention of child labour.

s4.title: Definitions
s4.item1: Any person under the age of 18.
s4.item2: Any adult who, by reason of disability, illness or circumstance, requires additional protection.
s4.item3: Any act or omission that causes physical, emotional, sexual, financial or psychological harm.
s4.item4: The proactive measures taken to protect people from harm.

s5.title: Recruitment and vetting
s5.p1: All mentors, volunteers and individuals offering placements may be subject to:
s5.item2: Reference checks (minimum two references for mentors);
s5.item3: A Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) where appropriate;
s5.item4: Interviews and a signed safeguarding declaration;

s6.title: Code of conduct
s6.item1: Treat others with dignity, fairness and respect;
s6.item2: Avoid any form of harassment, bullying, discrimination or exploitation;
s6.item3: Maintain appropriate professional boundaries at all times;
s6.item4: Never share or request explicit material;
s6.item5: Never provide alcohol, tobacco or illegal substances to a young person;
s6.item6: Never meet alone in private settings without prior approval and a parent/guardian's written consent.

s7.title: Mentoring guidelines
s7.item1: Mentoring sessions should take place in safe, public or supervised settings.
s7.item2: Online sessions should be conducted on approved platforms with appropriate adults aware.
s7.item3: Communication between mentors and minors must be transparent and copied to a parent/guardian where reasonable.
s7.item4: Mentors must not give or receive money, gifts of value or loans.
s7.item5: Any concern, however minor, must be reported to Hineni without delay.

s8.title: Apprenticeship and work placement standards
s8.item1: Placements must comply with South African labour legislation, including limits on the hours, conditions and types of work permitted for young workers.
s8.item2: Persons under 15 may not be employed. Persons aged 15–17 may only undertake suitable, age-appropriate work and only during school holidays unless otherwise lawfully permitted.
s8.item3: Health and safety risks must be assessed before any placement begins.
s8.item4: No young person may be exposed to hazardous machinery, chemicals, heights or work that could harm their physical or moral development.
s8.item5: Hosts must provide adequate supervision, induction and reasonable support throughout.
s8.item6: Hineni reserves the right to suspend or end any placement where standards are not met.

s9.title: Reporting concerns
s9.p1: Any concern, allegation or incident relating to a safeguarding matter must be reported immediately to Hineni:
s9.emergency: In an emergency, contact the South African Police Service (10111) or Childline South Africa (0800 055 555) first.

s10.title: Confidentiality
s10.p1: All reports are treated with appropriate confidentiality. Information is shared only with those who need it to protect the person at risk, and in accordance with POPIA and mandatory reporting duties under South African law.

s11.title: Digital safety
s11.item1: Personal data is processed in line with POPIA and Hineni's Privacy Notice.
s11.item2: Photos or videos of young people are only used with explicit, informed consent.
s11.item3: Users should not share personal contact details with strangers via the platform.
s11.item4: Suspicious accounts or messages must be reported to Hineni.

s12.title: Breaches and enforcement
s12.p1: Breaches of this policy may result in suspension, removal from the platform, referral to the relevant authorities and, where appropriate, criminal prosecution. Hineni cooperates fully with law-enforcement and statutory child-protection agencies.

s13.title: Disclaimer
s13.p1: Hineni undertakes reasonable verification, vetting and safeguarding measures. However, Hineni cannot guarantee the conduct of third parties and accepts no liability for injury, loss, damage, misconduct, criminal activity or disputes arising from interactions between participants, mentors, employers, apprenticeship providers or other users of the platform. Participation is undertaken at the individual's own risk and subject to applicable South African law.
